cards.text: This song comes from the sons of Korah, a family of Levites (2 Chronicles 20:19), and they skip the warm-up completely: "Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, His holy mountain." No small talk, friend, straight to the praise.

Then they start bragging on that mountain: Mount Zion is beautiful in loftiness, the joy of all the earth, like the peaks of Zaphon. They talk about it the way I talk about a tray of cookies fresh out of the oven, and friend, I do NOT stop talking.

cards.question: The song gives Mount Zion one more title. Whose city does it call Zion?

cards.text: Zion's got citadels, and in my bakery the only thing guarding the ovens is me and a mustache. The song says Zion's citadels have somebody WAY better than that.

cards.question: The song says Zion's own soldiers are the fortress in her citadels.

cards.text: Then this: "For behold, the kings assembled; they all advanced together." Not one king, friend, KINGS, plural, and I'd be checking every lock on the bakery door.

cards.question: The kings saw, and they were astounded. Then they ___ in terror.

cards.text: Trembling seizes them right there, anguish like a woman in labor. I know that tremble, friend: back when I was stuck in a junk drawer, I shook every time it opened, and all anybody wanted was the scissors.

cards.question: Then the song speaks right to God about the ships of Tarshish. What does it say God wrecked them with?

cards.text: Then the song says "we," and they start with what they had heard. The place they're talking about is the city of the LORD of Hosts, the city of our God.

cards.question: The song starts with what "we" had heard. What does it say they have done in the city of the LORD of Hosts?
The song says God will establish His city forever.

cards.text: Now the song slows WAY down and talks right to God. Inside His temple, the song says, "we contemplate" one thing about Him.

cards.question: Within God's temple, the song says what "we" contemplate is God's great power.
The song tells God that His name reaches a long way. How far?

answers.text: To the ends of the earth

cards.text: The song says God's right hand is full of righteousness. Then Mount Zion is glad, and the daughters of Judah rejoice right along with it.

cards.question: Mount Zion is glad and the daughters of Judah rejoice. What does the song say they rejoice on account of?

cards.text: Then the song gives an order: "March around Zion, encircle her, count her towers," then consider her ramparts and tour her citadels. I'm HOPPING that whole lap, gold base and all, but this tour isn't just for the people walking it.

cards.question: The song says to walk around Zion counting towers and touring citadels for a reason. What is it?

answers.text: So you can tell the next generation
So you can guard the city gates
So you can repair the old walls

cards.text: Then the song wraps up: "For this God is our God forever and ever…" Friend, I got swapped out once for a shinier stamper, so trust me, FOREVER and ever is the best news in this whole song.

cards.question: The song's last line says this God will be our guide even till death.
